## Environmental data
```{r env data}

#PAR -- Odyssey: shallow 2' = SN16333, intermediate 10' = SN16321, deep 22' = SN16315
#Temp -- Hobo: shallow 2' = 21556322, intermediate 10' = 21556332, deep 22' = 20970121

######## Temp compiling
# remove all unwanted rows and columns and split date and time column, grab files in a list
files <- list.files(path="data/environmental/temp", pattern = "csv$", full.names = T)
files

##### what are the file names, sans extensions
file.names<-file_path_sans_ext(list.files(path="data/environmental/temp", pattern = "csv$", full.names = F))
file.names

############ formatting all data in for loop
for(i in 1:length(files))
{
  data<-read.csv(files[i], header=F, stringsAsFactors=FALSE, sep=",", skip=1)
  df<-data[c(-1:-2),-1] # removes "trash" columns
  df<-df[, c(1:2)] # reorganize
  colnames(df)<-c("Date.time", "Temp")
  df$Raw.Temp<-as.numeric(as.character(df$Temp))
  df$timestamp<-mdy_hms(as.character(df$Date.time)) # corrects date format
  df$timestamp<-strptime(df$timestamp, format="%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S")
  df<- df %>% dplyr::select(timestamp, Temp) # remove old date-time column
  df<-df[!(df$timestamp < "2024-06-17 11:00:00 HST"),] # start at this time
  df<-df[!(df$timestamp > "2024-06-21 10:00:00 HST"),] # end at this time
  #df$SN<-file.names[i]
  #df$depth<-ifelse(file.names[i]=="20970121", "deep", "intermediate")
  #df$Date<-as.Date(df$timestamp)
  make.names(assign(paste("SN",file.names[i], sep=""), df)) # put pattern at front of names
}
# this is the end of the loop

ls()
files<-as.data.frame(mget(ls(pattern = "SN.*"))) # with SN as patterns in files from for loops
names(files) # see number of columns, and what these are
data_index<-c(1,(seq(2,4,2))) # these are the columns we will want: timestamp + raw data **change '18' to number of columns in your dataframe, specifying here to select 'every other column'

temps<-as.data.frame(c(files[, data_index])) # here is the data we want, now in df alone
colnames(temps)[1]="timestamp" # rename the single column for time


########## one logger had longer interval, adjust for this...
d.temp<-read.csv("data/environmental/temp/interval discrep/21556322.csv", 
                 header=F, stringsAsFactors=FALSE, sep=",", skip=1)
  df<-d.temp[c(-1:-2),-1] # removes "trash" columns
  df<-df[, c(1:2)] # reorganize
  colnames(df)<-c("Date.time", "SN21556322.Temp")
  df$SN21556322.Temp<-as.numeric(as.character(df$SN21556322.Temp))
  df$timestamp<-mdy_hms(as.character(df$Date.time)) # corrects date format
  df$timestamp<-strptime(df$timestamp, format="%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S")
  df<- df %>% dplyr::select(timestamp, SN21556322.Temp) # remove old date-time column
  df<-df[!(df$timestamp < "2024-06-17 11:00:00 HST"),] # start at this time
  df<-df[!(df$timestamp > "2024-06-21 10:00:00 HST"),] # end at this time
  df$timestamp<-as.POSIXct(df$timestamp)
  SN21556322<-df


# combine all data based on time, gives hourly values for all loggers
df.all.temp <- merge(temps, SN21556322, by= "timestamp", na.rm=TRUE)
df.all.temp<-na.omit(df.all.temp) # remove NA
write.csv(df.all.temp, "output/Temp_hourly_light.depth.KBay.csv")

# reorganize to 2 columns
#df.all.temp$Date<-as.Date(df.all.temp$timestamp)
shal.T<-df.all.temp %>% dplyr::select(timestamp, SN21556322.Temp)
shal.T$depth<-"shallow"; shal.T$SN<-"SN21556322"
shal.T <- shal.T %>%  dplyr::rename("Temp.C" = "SN21556322.Temp")

inter.T<-df.all.temp %>% dplyr::select(timestamp, SN21556332.Temp)
inter.T$depth<-"intermed"; inter.T$SN<-"SN21556332"
inter.T <- inter.T %>%  dplyr::rename("Temp.C" = "SN21556332.Temp")

deep.T<-df.all.temp %>% dplyr::select(timestamp, SN20970121.Temp)
deep.T$depth<-"deep"; deep.T$SN<-"SN20970121"
deep.T <- deep.T %>%  dplyr::rename("Temp.C" = "SN20970121.Temp")

Temp.long<-rbind(shal.T, inter.T, deep.T)
Temp.long$Date<-as.Date(Temp.long$timestamp)
Temp.long$Temp.C<-as.numeric(Temp.long$Temp.C)
Temp.long$depth<-as.factor(Temp.long$depth)

Temp.long$depth<-factor(Temp.long$depth, levels=c("shallow", "intermed", "deep"))
Temp.long$depth.m<- ifelse(Temp.long$depth=="shallow", "<1m", 
                          ifelse(Temp.long$depth=="intermed", "3m", "7m"))

############ plot the temp data
temp.plot<-ggplot(Temp.long, aes(x=timestamp, y=Temp.C, color=depth.m)) + 
  geom_line(lwd=0.7) + 
  geom_point(size=1.5) +
  scale_color_manual(values=c("lightseagreen", "royalblue", "slategray4")) +
  xlab("Date") +
  ylab("Hourly Temperature (°C)") +
  Fig.formatting

temp.plot
dev.copy(pdf, "figures/Temp.plot.pdf", width = 6, height = 6)
dev.off()
```

```{r light data}
##### grab files in a list
PAR.files <- list.files(path="data/environmental/light", pattern = "CSV$", full.names = T); PAR.files

##### what are the file names, sans extensions
file.names<-file_path_sans_ext(list.files(path="data/environmental/light", pattern = "CSV$", full.names = F))

############ formatting all data in for loop
for(i in 1:length(PAR.files))
{
  data<-read.csv(PAR.files[i], sep=",", skip=8)
  df<-data[, -1] # removes "trash" columns
  colnames(df)<-c("Date", "Time", "Raw.PAR", "Cal.PAR")
  df$Date<-dmy(df$Date) # corrects date format
  df$timestamp<-as.POSIXct(paste(df$Date, df$Time), format="%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S")
  df<- df %>%  dplyr::select(Date, timestamp, Cal.PAR) # timestamp and Raw value only
  df<-df[!(df$timestamp < "2024-06-17 12:00:00"),] # start at this time
  df<-df[!(df$timestamp >= "2024-06-21 10:00:00"),] # end at this time
  make.names(assign(paste("SN.Od",file.names[i], sep=""), df)) # put pattern at front of names
  # makes each df[i] as dataframe with specific file-name
  # write.csv(df.out, file=paste("trim",file.names[i])) # makes .csvs for output
}
# this is the end of the loop

########## see the files you've made, as a list, then grab those that fill your pattern 
ls()
files<-as.data.frame(mget(ls(pattern = "SN.Od.*"))) # with SN as patterns in files from for loops
names(files) # see number of columns, and what these are

data_index<-c(1:2,(seq(3,9,3))) # these are the columns we will want: timestamp + raw data **change '18' to number of columns in your dataframe, specifying here to select 'every other column'

PAR<-as.data.frame(c(files[, data_index])) # here is the data we want, now in df alone
names(PAR) = gsub(pattern = "_.*", replacement = "", x = names(PAR)) #strip name to SN only
colnames(PAR)[1]="Date" # rename the single column for time
colnames(PAR)[2]="timestamp"

# export
PAR.export<-PAR
colnames(PAR.export)<- c("Date", "timestamp", "SN16315.deep", "SN16321.interm", "SN16333.shal")
write.csv(PAR.export, "output/PAR_light.depth.KBay.csv")

###### change format for ggplotting
PAR.shal<- PAR.export %>% dplyr::select("Date", "timestamp", "SN16333.shal") 
  PAR.shal$depth<-"shallow"; PAR.shal$SN<-"SN16333"; colnames(PAR.shal)[3]<-"PAR"
PAR.interm<- PAR.export %>% dplyr::select("Date", "timestamp", "SN16321.interm")
  PAR.interm$depth<- "intermed" ; PAR.interm$SN<-"SN16321"; colnames(PAR.interm)[3]<-"PAR"
PAR.deep<- PAR.export %>% dplyr::select("Date", "timestamp", "SN16315.deep")
  PAR.deep$depth<-"deep"; PAR.deep$SN<-"SN16315"; colnames(PAR.deep)[3]<-"PAR"

PAR.long<-rbind(PAR.shal, PAR.interm, PAR.deep)
PAR.long$PAR<-as.numeric(PAR.long$PAR)
PAR.long$depth<-as.factor(PAR.long$depth)
PAR.long$depth.m<- ifelse(PAR.long$depth=="shallow", "<1m", 
                          ifelse(PAR.long$depth=="intermed", "3m", "7m"))

PAR.long$depth<-factor(PAR.long$depth, levels=c("shallow", "intermed", "deep"))

############ plot the PAR data: note unites are umol photons m-2 s-1 at 10 min interval
PAR.plot<-ggplot(PAR.long, aes(x=timestamp, y=PAR, color=depth.m)) + 
  geom_line(lwd=0.7) + 
  geom_point(size=1.5, alpha=0.5) +
  ylim(0,2000)+
  scale_color_manual(values=c("coral2", "khaki3", "indianred4")) +
  xlab("Date") +
  ylab(expression(paste("PAR", mu,"mol photons", ~m^-2, ~s^-1, sep="")))+
  Fig.formatting

######### DLI
df.split <- split(PAR.export, f=PAR.export$timestamp
                  < as.Date("2024-06-18", format="%F")) # split df by date

# interval is 10min, logging a value at 1 sec. 
# Approach 1: Calculate as DLI from instantaneous values...
# 60s*60m = (3600), *24h day *values /10^6 = 0.0864 light over full day. 
# If only "light interval" then specify # of hours in the day (seasonal specific)

# Approach 2: Summing over day and calcualte from logging interval 
# sum values over day and multiply by logging interval * seconds in minute (10min * 60sec), divide by 10^6

# approach 1
df.dli<-aggregate(data.frame(shal.DLI=df.split[[1]]$SN16333.shal*0.0864,
                             intermed.DLI=df.split[[1]]$SN16321.interm*0.0864,
                             deep.DLI=df.split[[1]]$SN16315.deep*0.0864),
                  by=list(Date=df.split[[1]]$Date), FUN=mean)

# approach 2 (just to keep us honest)
df.dli2<-aggregate(data.frame(shal.DLI=df.split[[1]]$SN16333.shal,
                             intermed.DLI=df.split[[1]]$SN16321.interm,
                             deep.DLI=df.split[[1]]$SN16315.deep),
                  by=list(Date=df.split[[1]]$Date), FUN=sum)
df.dli2$sh<-df.dli2$shal.DLI*(10*60)/1000000
df.dli2$int<-df.dli2$intermed.DLI*(10*60)/1000000
df.dli2$dp<-df.dli2$deep.DLI*(10*60)/1000000

# # remove dates without full 24 h deployment 
df.dli<-df.dli[!(df.dli$Date=="2024-06-17"), ] 
df.dli<-df.dli[!(df.dli$Date >="2024-06-21"), ]


## combine dataframe
shall.DLI.df<-df.dli %>% dplyr::select (Date, shal.DLI); colnames(shall.DLI.df)[2]<- "DLI"
  shall.DLI.df$depth<- "shallow"
intermed.DLI.df<-df.dli %>% dplyr::select (Date, intermed.DLI); colnames(intermed.DLI.df)[2]<- "DLI"
  intermed.DLI.df$depth<- "intermed"
deep.DLI.df<-df.dli %>% dplyr::select (Date, deep.DLI); colnames(deep.DLI.df)[2]<- "DLI"
   deep.DLI.df$depth<- "deep"
DLI.bind<-rbind(shall.DLI.df,intermed.DLI.df,deep.DLI.df)

DLI.bind$depth.m<- ifelse(DLI.bind$depth=="shallow", "<1m", 
                          ifelse(DLI.bind$depth=="intermed", "3m", "7m"))

DLI.bind$depth<-factor(DLI.bind$depth, levels=c("shallow", "intermed", "deep"))

aggregate(DLI~depth, data=DLI.bind, FUN=mean)

############ plot the DLI data: note unites are mole photons m-2 d-1 at 10 min interval
DLI.plot<-ggplot(DLI.bind, aes(x=depth.m, y=DLI, fill=depth)) + 
  geom_boxplot(alpha=0.9) +
  geom_point(size=2, alpha=0.5, aes(fill=depth)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values=c("coral2", "khaki3", "indianred4")) +
  xlab("Depth bin") +
  ylab(expression(paste("DLI (mol photons", ~m^-2, ~d^-1,")", sep="")))+
  Fig.formatting

env.plots<-plot_grid(temp.plot, PAR.plot, DLI.plot+guides(fill="none"),
                            ncol=3, nrow=1, rel_widths = c(10,10,6))
env.plots
dev.copy(pdf, "figures/Figx.Temp.PAR.DLI.pdf", width = 12, height = 4)
dev.off()

```

## Phys data
```{r phys}
phys.df<-read.csv("data/ESVI_PhysIso_pooledphys.csv")

# make a meter column
phys.df<- phys.df %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(depth.m = depth.ft*0.3048)

#calculate variables
# total chlorophyll / cm2
phys.df$chlcm2<-(phys.df$total.chl.ug.ml*phys.df$blastate.ml)/phys.df$surface.area.cm2

# total biomass mg AFDW/ cm2
phys.df$AFDW<- ((phys.df$biomass.g.ml*1000)*phys.df$blastate.ml)/phys.df$surface.area.cm2

phys.df$depth.bin<-ifelse(phys.df$depth.ft<7, "shallow",
                    ifelse(phys.df$depth.ft>20, "deep", "intermediate"))

phys.df$depth.bin<-factor(phys.df$depth.bin, levels=c("shallow", "intermediate", "deep"))
                    
phys.df<- phys.df %>%
  dplyr::select(species, sample.ID, site, depth.m, depth.bin, chlcm2, AFDW)

###### plots
# chl
chl.bin<-ggplot(phys.df, aes(depth.bin, chlcm2)) +
  facet_wrap(.~species)+
  geom_boxplot(fill= "goldenrod", outlier.size = 0.7, alpha=0.5)+
  ylab(expression(paste("total chlorophyll", " (\U00B5g/cm"^2, ")")))+
  xlab("depth bin")+ theme_bw() +
  theme(strip.text = element_text(face = "italic"))

# AFDW
biomass.bin<-ggplot(phys.df, aes(depth.bin, AFDW)) +
  facet_wrap(.~species)+
  geom_boxplot(fill= "goldenrod4", outlier.size = 0.7, alpha=0.5)+
  ylab(expression(paste("AFDW", " (mg/cm"^2, ")")))+
  xlab("depth bin")+ theme_bw() +
  theme(strip.text = element_text(face = "italic"))

###### summary stats
AFDW.mean<-aggregate(AFDW~depth.bin*species, data=phys.df, FUN=mean)
AFDW.se<-aggregate(AFDW~depth.bin*species, data=phys.df, FUN=std.error)
AFDW.n<-aggregate(AFDW~depth.bin*species, data=phys.df, FUN=length)

AFDW.sum<-cbind(AFDW.mean, AFDW.se[3], AFDW.n[3])
colnames(AFDW.sum)<-c("depth.bin", "species", "AFDW.mean", "SE", "n")

#
chl.mean<-aggregate(chlcm2~depth.bin*species, data=phys.df, FUN=mean)
chl.se<-aggregate(chlcm2~depth.bin*species, data=phys.df, FUN=std.error)
chl.n<-aggregate(chlcm2~depth.bin*species, data=phys.df, FUN=length)

chl.sum<-cbind(chl.mean, chl.se[3], chl.n[3])
colnames(chl.sum)<-c("depth.bin", "species", "chl.mean", "SE", "n")

# set dodge parameters
dodge = position_dodge(width = 0.40)

## dot mean and SE plot
chl.dot.mean.plot<- ggplot(chl.sum, aes(y=chl.mean, x=depth.bin)) +
  facet_wrap(.~species)+
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = chl.mean-SE, ymax = chl.mean+SE), 
                position = dodge, width = 0.0, linewidth = 0.75, color="gray20") +
  geom_point(color="goldenrod", size=4, alpha=0.8)+
  ylim(0,15)+
  ylab(expression(paste("total chlorophyll", " (\U00B5g/cm"^2, ")")))+
  xlab("depth bin")+ theme_bw() +
  theme(strip.text = element_text(face = "italic"))

## dot mean and SE plot
AFDW.dot.mean.plot<-ggplot(AFDW.sum, aes(y=AFDW.mean, x=depth.bin)) +
  facet_wrap(.~species)+
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = AFDW.mean-SE, ymax = AFDW.mean+SE), 
                position = dodge, width = 0.0, linewidth = 0.75, color="gray20") +
  geom_point(color="goldenrod4", size=4, alpha=0.8)+
  ylim(0,10)+
  ylab(expression(paste("AFDW", " (mg/cm"^2, ")")))+
  xlab("depth bin")+ theme_bw() +
  theme(strip.text = element_text(face = "italic"))

plot_grid(chl.dot.mean.plot, AFDW.dot.mean.plot, ncol=2)
dev.print(pdf, "figures/phys.plots1.pdf", width=10, height=3)
dev.off()
```

```{r}
MC.phys<-phys.df [(phys.df$species=="M. capitata"),]
PC.phys<-phys.df [(phys.df$species=="P. compressa"),]

### Chl and AFDW model discrete and continuous
####### MC
chl.mod.MC<-lm(chlcm2~depth.bin, data=MC.phys)
anova(chl.mod.MC) #NS

chl.mod.cont.MC<-lm(chlcm2~depth.m, data=MC.phys)
anova(chl.mod.cont.MC) #NS

### AFDW model discrete and continuous
AFDW.mod.MC<-lm(AFDW~depth.bin, data=MC.phys)
anova(AFDW.mod.MC) # NS

AFDW.mod.cont.MC<-lm(AFDW~depth.m, data=MC.phys)
anova(AFDW.mod.cont.MC) #NS

####### 
### Chl and AFDW model discrete and continuous
####### PC
chl.mod.PC<-lm(chlcm2~depth.bin, data=PC.phys)
anova(chl.mod.PC) #NS

chl.mod.cont.PC<-lm(chlcm2~depth.m, data=PC.phys)
anova(chl.mod.cont.PC) #NS

### AFDW model discrete and continuous
AFDW.mod.PC<-lm(AFDW~depth.bin, data=PC.phys)
anova(AFDW.mod.PC) # NS

AFDW.mod.cont.PC<-lm(AFDW~depth.m, data=PC.phys)
anova(AFDW.mod.cont.PC) #NS
```

## Bulk tissue EA analysis
```{r bulk}
bulk.df.OG<-read.csv("data/ESVI_bulk iso_long.csv")
bulk.df<-bulk.df.OG[!(bulk.df.OG$sample.ID=="MC03" & bulk.df.OG$fraction=="host"),] # odd d15N outlier, remove

# make a meter column
bulk.df<- bulk.df %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(depth.m = depth.ft*0.3048)

bulk.df$depth.bin<-ifelse(bulk.df$depth.ft<7, "shallow",
                    ifelse(bulk.df$depth.ft>20, "deep", "intermediate"))

bulk.df$depth.bin<-factor(bulk.df$depth.bin, levels=c("shallow", "intermediate", "deep"))
                    

# format metadata
make.fac<-c("species", "fraction", "sample.ID")
bulk.df[make.fac]<-lapply(bulk.df[make.fac], factor) # make all these factors

EA.df<-bulk.df %>%
  dplyr::select(species, depth.m, depth.bin, fraction, ug.N, d15N, ug.C, d13C, C.N.mol)

# figures
d13C.bin<-ggplot(EA.df, aes(depth.bin, d13C, fill=fraction)) +
  facet_wrap(.~species)+
  geom_boxplot(outlier.size = 0.7, alpha=0.5)+
  scale_fill_manual(values=c("gray50", "goldenrod")) +
  ylab(expression(paste(delta^{13}, C, " (\u2030)")))+
  xlab("depth bin")+ theme_bw() +
  theme(strip.text = element_text(face = "italic"))

d13C.depth<-ggplot(EA.df, aes(y=d13C, x=depth.m, color=fraction)) +
  facet_wrap(.~species)+
  geom_point()+
  scale_color_manual(values=c("gray50", "goldenrod")) +
  scale_fill_manual(values=c("gray50", "goldenrod")) +
  geom_smooth(method=lm, aes(fill=fraction)) +
  ylab(expression(paste(delta^{13}, C, " (\u2030)")))+
  xlab("depth (m)")+ theme_bw() +
  theme(strip.text = element_text(face = "italic"))

MC.d13C.density<- ggplot(EA.df[(EA.df$species=="Mcapitata"),] , aes(d13C, fill=fraction)) + 
  facet_wrap(.~depth.bin)+
  geom_density(alpha=.5) + 
  scale_fill_manual(values = c('gray50','goldenrod')) + xlim(-20, -12) + 
  ggtitle(expression(italic("M. capitata"))) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "italic")) +
  xlab(expression(paste(delta^{13}, C, " (\u2030)"))) + theme_bw()

PC.d13C.density<- ggplot(EA.df[(EA.df$species=="Pcompressa"),] , aes(d13C, fill=fraction)) + 
  facet_wrap(.~depth.bin)+
  geom_density(alpha=.5) + 
  scale_fill_manual(values = c('gray50','goldenrod')) + xlim(-20, -12) + 
  ggtitle(expression(italic("P. compressa"))) +
  xlab(expression(paste(delta^{13}, C, " (\u2030)"))) + theme_bw()


d15N.bin<-ggplot(EA.df, aes(depth.bin, d15N, fill=fraction)) +
  facet_wrap(.~species)+
  geom_boxplot(outlier.size = 0.7, alpha=0.5)+
  scale_fill_manual(values=c("gray50", "seagreen")) +
  ylab(expression(paste(delta^{15}, N, " (\u2030)")))+
  xlab("depth bin")+
  theme(strip.text = element_text(face = "italic")) +theme_bw()

d15N.depth<-ggplot(EA.df, aes(y=d15N, x=depth.m, color=fraction)) +
  facet_wrap(.~species)+
  geom_point()+
  scale_fill_manual(values=c("gray50", "seagreen")) +
  scale_color_manual(values=c("gray50", "seagreen")) +
  geom_smooth(method=lm, aes(fill=fraction)) +
  ylab(expression(paste(delta^{15}, N, " (\u2030)")))+
  theme(strip.text = element_text(face = "italic")) +
  xlab("depth (m)")+ theme_bw()
```

## SIBER
Use δ^13^C and δ^15^N biplots and perform `SIBER: Stable Isotope Bayesian Ellipse in R` analysis. This will plot the raw data with the standardized ellispe area, with 40% probability. This calculates the Isotope Niche Width.
```{r Siber, fig.show='hide', results='hide'}
### BULK d13C-d15N BIPLOT AND STANDARD ELLIPSES### 

# load the SIBER package: library(SIBER)
# load the data: library(dplyr)

# load bulk data from above = 'EA.df'
MC.df<-EA.df[(EA.df$species=="Mcapitata"),]
PC.df<-EA.df[(EA.df$species=="Pcompressa"),]

# subset to be only bulk d13C and d15N
bulk.siber<- EA.df %>%
  dplyr::select(d13C, d15N, fraction, species)

all.siber.data<- bulk.siber %>%  dplyr::rename(iso1 = d13C, iso2 = d15N, group=fraction, community=species)

# filter for each species 
MC.siber.data<- all.siber.data %>%
  filter(community =="Mcapitata")
PC.siber.data<- all.siber.data %>%
  filter(community =="Pcompressa")

# droplevels
MC.siber.data$community<-droplevels(MC.siber.data$community)
PC.siber.data$community<-droplevels(PC.siber.data$community)

# Create the SIBER object
all.siber<- createSiberObject(all.siber.data)
MC.siber <- createSiberObject(MC.siber.data)
PC.siber <- createSiberObject(PC.siber.data)

# for Hotelling things
hotellings.data <- data.frame(
  group = as.numeric(as.factor(all.siber.data$group)),
  x = all.siber.data$iso1,
  y = all.siber.data$iso2)

hotellings.MC.data <- data.frame(
  group = as.numeric(as.factor(MC.siber.data$group)),
  x = MC.siber.data$iso1,
  y = MC.siber.data$iso2)

hotellings.PC.data <- data.frame(
  group = as.numeric(as.factor(PC.siber.data$group)),
  x = PC.siber.data$iso1,
  y = PC.siber.data$iso2)


########### ellipses
community.hulls.args <- list(col = 1, lty = 1, lwd = 1)
group.ellipses.args2  <- list(n = 100, p.interval = 0.95, lty = 1, lwd = 2)
group.ellipses.args  <- list(n = 100, p.interval = 0.40, lty = 1, lwd = 2) #Standard ellipse
group.hulls.args     <- list(lty = 2)

# ellipses and group.hulls are set to TRUE or T for short to force their plotting
palette(c("coral", "dodgerblue"))
par(mfrow=c(1,1))
plotSiberObject(MC.siber,
                ax.pad = 2, 
                hulls = F, community.hulls.args, 
                ellipses = T, group.ellipses.args,
                group.hulls = T, group.hulls.args,
                bty = "L",
                iso.order = c(1,2),
                xlab = expression({delta}^13*C~'‰'),
                ylab = expression({delta}^15*N~'‰'),
                x.limits=c(-20.0, -14),
                y.limits = c(2, 8)
)
mtext("40% SEAc = 63% \n 95% MEAc = 97%", side = 3, line = 0, cex = 0.75)

```

Calculate the posterior estimates of the `Bayesian Standard Ellipse Area (SEA~B~)`. We will add this to the SIBER biplot generated above. The SEA~B~ plot shows the  95%, 75%, and 50% credible intervals for each species, with modes indicated by black circles.

Calculate summary statistics for each group: TA, SEA and SEAc
```{r}
# * note sensitivity to sample size for n < 10 such that small sample sizes typically result in underestimation of the population TA

# TA = total area of the convex hull, (TA) is highly sensitive to sample size and increases with sample size.

## SEA asymptotes quickly to a constant value (in this case p, as both a and b = 1), at around n = 30. The underestimation of the population SEA for small sample sizes is an undesirable property, as it is likely to confound comparisons between studies with unequal sample sizes.

# SEA-c: calculation of a corrected standard ellipse based on low sample size

# SEA-b: The Bayesian estimate captures all the same properties as SEAc, being unbiased with respect to sample size and exhibiting more uncertainty with smaller sample size.

group.ML.MC <- groupMetricsML(MC.siber)
print(group.ML.MC)

group.ML.PC<- groupMetricsML(PC.siber)
print(group.ML.PC)
```

After calling siberMVN() you will see output in the command window indicating that the jags models are being fitted, one block of output for each group in your dataset. 

```{r Siber JAGS}
# options for running jags
parms <- list()
parms$n.iter <- 2 * 10^4   # number of iterations to run the model for
parms$n.burnin <- 1 * 10^3 # discard the first set of values
parms$n.thin <- 10     # thin the posterior by this many
parms$n.chains <- 2        # run this many chains

# define the priors
priors <- list()
priors$R <- 1 * diag(2)
priors$k <- 2
priors$tau.mu <- 1.0E-3

# fit the ellipses which uses an Inverse Wishart prior
# on the covariance matrix Sigma, and a vague normal prior on the 
# means. Fitting is via the JAGS method.
MC.ellipses.posterior <- siberMVN(MC.siber, parms, priors)
PC.ellipses.posterior <- siberMVN(PC.siber, parms, priors)
```

When comparing individual groups with each other, be it within a single community, or groups among communities, the `Standard Ellipse Area (SEA)` is the recommended method. 

Since the multivariate normal distributions have already been fitted to each group, it only remains to calculate the SEA on the posterior distribution of covariance matrix for each group, thereby yielding the `Bayesian SEA or SEA-B`. 

We can also use the summary statistics we calculated earlier to add the maximum likelihood estimates of `SEA-c` to the Bayesian estimates. Credible intervals can be extracted by calling the function hdr from the hdrcde package.

```{r SEAb}
# The posterior estimates of the ellipses for each group can be used to
# calculate the SEA.B for each group with probs = c(95, 75, 50)
SEA.B.MC <- siberEllipses(MC.ellipses.posterior)

my_clrs <- matrix(c("salmon2", "coral", "red2","powderblue", "turquoise", "turquoise3"), nrow = 3, ncol = 2)

siberDensityPlot(SEA.B.MC, xticklabels = colnames(group.ML.MC), 
                xlab = c("Community | Group"),
                ylab = expression("SEA "[B]~ ('\u2030' ^2) ),
                bty = "L",
                las = 1,
                ylim = c(0,4),
                main = "SIBER ellipse: M compressa",
                clr = my_clrs)

# Add red x's for the ML estimated SEA-c
points(1:ncol(SEA.B.MC), group.ML.MC[3,], col="black", pch = "x", lwd = 3)

#SEAb.plot.MC<- recordPlot()
dev.copy(pdf, "figures/SEAb.plot.MC.pdf", height=7, width=5)
dev.off()

######################
SEA.B.PC <- siberEllipses(PC.ellipses.posterior)

siberDensityPlot(SEA.B.PC, xticklabels = colnames(group.ML.PC), 
                xlab = c("Community | Group"),
                ylab = expression("SEA "[B]~ ('\u2030' ^2) ),
                bty = "L",
                las = 1,
                ylim = c(0,4),
                main = "SIBER ellipses: P compressa",
                clr = my_clrs)

# Add black x's for the ML estimated SEA-c
points(1:ncol(SEA.B.PC), group.ML.PC[3,], col="black", pch = "x", lwd = 3)

#SEAb.plot.PC<- recordPlot()
dev.copy(pdf, "figures/SEAb.plot.PC.pdf", height=7, width=5)
dev.off()

```

One can calculate the overlap between two (or more) ellipses. In the first instance, this overlap is simply the area, in units of per mil squared, contained by the shape that lies within the overlapping region. This overlap is most easily calculated by using the *SEAc* of each ellipse.

The proportion of overlap is calculated as per Conti-Jerpe 2020:
*...as the proportion of the host SEAc that the total overlap accounts for.* = overlap/host-SEAc

The overlap between the SEAc for groups 1.2 and 1.3 is given by:
```{r}
############ 40% overlap = SEAc
### Mcap
overlap.G1.2.G1.3.MC <- maxLikOverlap("Mcapitata.host", "Mcapitata.symbiont", MC.siber, p = 0.40, n =)

prop.of.first.MC <- as.numeric(overlap.G1.2.G1.3.MC["overlap"] / overlap.G1.2.G1.3.MC["area.1"])
print(prop.of.first.MC) # 63% overlap = proportion of total overlap relative to the host SEAc 

prop.of.second.MC <- as.numeric(overlap.G1.2.G1.3.MC["overlap"] / overlap.G1.2.G1.3.MC["area.2"])
print(prop.of.second.MC) # 46% overlap = = proportion of total overlap relative to the symbiont SEAc 

### Pcomp
overlap.G1.2.G1.3.PC <- maxLikOverlap("Pcompressa.host", "Pcompressa.symbiont", PC.siber, p = 0.40, n =)

prop.of.first.PC <- as.numeric(overlap.G1.2.G1.3.PC["overlap"] / overlap.G1.2.G1.3.PC["area.1"])
print(prop.of.first.PC) # 94% overlap host with symbiont


############ 95% overlap = "Major ellipse area"  = MEA
### Mcap
overlap.G1.2.G1.3.MC <- maxLikOverlap("Mcapitata.host", "Mcapitata.symbiont", MC.siber, p = 0.95, n =)

prop.of.first.MC <- as.numeric(overlap.G1.2.G1.3.MC["overlap"] / overlap.G1.2.G1.3.MC["area.1"])
print(prop.of.first.MC) # 84% overlap host with symbiont


### Pcomp
overlap.G1.2.G1.3.PC <- maxLikOverlap("Pcompressa.host", "Pcompressa.symbiont", PC.siber, p = 0.95, n =)

prop.of.first.PC <- as.numeric(overlap.G1.2.G1.3.PC["overlap"] / overlap.G1.2.G1.3.PC["area.1"])
print(prop.of.first.PC) # 97% overlap host with symbiont

```
*Montipora capitata* = 63% overlap (Host-SEAc), 84% (Host-MEAc)
*Porites compressa* = 94% overlap (Host-SEAc), 97% (Host-MEAc)

```{r Turner, eval=FALSE}
source('scripts/Turner.et.al.ecology.source.r')

# set df here
# PC.df
# MC.df

#headings of columns in .csv must be "group", "x", and "y", where x = d13C
Turn.df<-PC.df %>% dplyr::select(fraction, d13C, d15N)
colnames(Turn.df)<-c("group", "x", "y")

Y<-as.matrix(Turn.df[,2:3])

# Designate groups
group<-as.factor(Turn.df[,1])
gp<-length(levels(group)) # number of groups
n.comp<-(gp^2-gp)/2 # number of possible comparisons
rownames(Y)<-group 

lm.gp<-lm(Y~group,x=T,model=T) # for estimating group means
#This outputs the centroid of one group and distance in x and y to the centroid of the second group

res.gp<-resid(lm.gp) # residuals of groups from group means
yhat.gp<-predict(lm.gp) # predicted values

lm.gp.red<-lm(Y~1) # this is the model reduced by the group factor: only estimates an overall mean

#PLOTS

par(mai=c(1,1,0.5,0.5))

Trophic.1<-Turn.df[Turn.df$group=="host",2:3]
Trophic.2<-Turn.df[Turn.df$group=="symbiont",2:3]
All.pts<-rbind(Trophic.1,Trophic.2)


plot(All.pts,type='n',asp=1,xlab=expression(delta^13~C),ylab=expression(delta^15~N),cex.lab=1.7,cex.axis=1.7)
points(Trophic.1, pch=21,bg="coral") # host
points(Trophic.2, pch=21,bg="dodgerblue") # symbiont
Trophic.1.c<-colMeans(Trophic.1)
Trophic.2.c<-colMeans(Trophic.2)

points(Trophic.1.c[1],Trophic.1.c[2], pch=21,bg="coral",cex=1.7,lwd=2.5) # centroid = x (-16.606667), y (4.273333) 
points(Trophic.2.c[1],Trophic.2.c[2], pch=21,bg="dodgerblue",cex=1.7,lwd=2.5) # centroid = x (-16.520000), y (4.466667) 


######## DISPERSION MEASURES: MDC, MNN, ECC
#mdc = mean centroid distance
#mnn = mean nearest neighbor
#ecc = eccentricity

ex1<-ds.prep(res.gp,group) # see source file
ex1.ds<-disp.stat(ex1) # see source file
ex1.ds

# GROUP MEANS
gp.m<-group.means(Y,group) # finds the group means for the raw data
gp.m

# CONTRASTS
mean.dif<-as.vector(dist(as.matrix(gp.m)))
mean.dif

disp.dif<-ds.dif(ex1.ds) # Dimension names not given by output

disp.dif 
disp.dif$mdc
disp.dif$mnn
disp.dif$ecc

#### PERMUTATION PROCEDURE ####

# Describe a function that needs
# x = the full linear model
# x2 = the reduced linear model
# y = the raw data
# g = group list
# p = the number of permutations to use (keep in mind that
# the observed values count as 1 random permutation)

# SETUP
permute<-function(x,x2,y,g,p){
  p.table<-NULL
  
  yhat<-predict(x)
  res<-resid(x)
  line<-nrow(res) # this defines the number of permutable objects
  yhat.2<-predict(x2)
  res.2<-resid(x2)
  
  mean.dif<-as.vector(dist(as.matrix(group.means(Y,g))))
  
  
  for(i in 1:p){
    
    #For dispersion tests
    
    line.rand<-sample(line,replace=FALSE) # This creates a line from 1 to the number
    # of permutable objects, then randomizes the order
    res.temp<-cbind(line.rand,res) # attaches the random order to the ordered matrix
    z<-(order(line.rand)) # randomizes matrix as it reorders line
    res.temp2<-as.matrix(res.temp[z,])# removes randomized line
    res.p<-res.temp2[,-1] # Rows of residuals are now randomized
    y.rand<-yhat+res.p # random values created
    
    # The resampling procedure above is the same as randomizing original values
    # (Since the reduced model only contains the overall mean)
    # But using residuals makes it applicable to multi-factor models
    
    lm.r<-lm(y.rand~g,x=T,model=T) # new linear model
    r<-resid(lm.r)
    yhat<-predict(lm.r)
    ex1.r<-ds.prep(r,g) #thanks to the functions, prep takes one step
    ex.r.ds<-disp.stat(ex1.r) # thanks to the function, dispersion stats require one step
    disp.dif.r<-ds.dif(ex.r.ds) # thanks to function, contrasts require one step
    
    
    # For means tests
    
    # uses different linear model
    # the null hypothesis that means are equal
    # means that an intercept model (i.e., defines only the overall mean)
    # is as viable as a group means model.
    # Thus, residuals are calculated from the intercept model (see above)
    # and random means are created despite no mean differences define by the model
    # this creates random distibutions of outcomes under the null hypothesis
    
    res.2.temp<-cbind(line.rand,res.2)
    z<-(order(line.rand))
    res.2.temp2<-as.matrix(res.2.temp[z,])
    res.2.p<-res.temp2[,-1] # Rows of residuals are now randomized
    y.rand.2<-yhat.2+res.2.p
    
    
    gm.r<-group.means(y.rand.2,g)
    md.r<-as.vector(dist(as.matrix(gm.r)))
    
    result<-c(i,md.r,disp.dif.r$mdc,disp.dif.r$mnn,disp.dif.r$ecc) # bind all results together
    p.table<-rbind(p.table,result) # add them to a table, row by row
    
  }
  
  head<-NULL # create a header
  line1<-as.vector(c(0,mean.dif,disp.dif$mdc,disp.dif$mnn,disp.dif$ecc))
  
  # The following is a bunch of code simply for generating column names in the output
  
  cn<-length(mean.dif) # cn = column name
  
  test.list<-NULL
  if (cn>1) for(i in 1:cn){
    l1<-rep(i,cn)
    l2<-array(1:cn)
    l12<-cbind(l1,l2)
    test.list<-rbind(test.list,l12)
  }
  
  test.list2<-NULL
  if (cn>1) for(j in 1:nrow(test.list)){
    t<-test.list[j,]
    if(t[2]>t[1]) test.list2<-rbind(test.list2,t)
  }
  
  test.list3<-NULL
  if (cn>1) for(k in 1:nrow(test.list2)){
    t<-test.list2[k,]
    lab<-paste(t[1],t[2],sep="--")
    test.list3<-rbind(test.list3,lab)}
  
  if (cn==1) test.list3<-c("1--2")
  
  lab2<-c(rep("MD",cn),rep("MDC",cn),rep("MNN",cn),rep("ECC",cn))
  test.list4<-paste(lab2,test.list3,sep=".")
  
  head<-c("iteration",test.list4)
  p.table<-rbind(head,line1,p.table)
  
}


test1<-permute(lm.gp,lm.gp.red,Y,group,999) # run the permutation test

# results can be opened in e.g., excel. 
# Find the P-value by measuring the rank of the first value in the distribution of values in the same column.  
# p.table.out<-test1
# write.csv(p.table.out,"output/ACRO_results.csv") 
# Alternatvely, more R-code can
# be generated to calculate P-values by using a function that ranks observed values
# see below

# P-Values
h<-test1[1,];h<-h[-1]
t<-test1[-1,];t<-t[,-1]
f<-function(t){
  r<-rank(t)
  p<-r[1]
  c<-length(t)
  pv<-(c-p+1)/c}
p.value<-apply(t,2,f)
names(p.value)<-h

p.value


#ADDENDUM: HOTELLING'S T2
#Each group comparison one at a time

#Comparing groups 1 (host) and 2 (symbiont) 
gp.m.dif<-gp.m[1,]-gp.m[2,] # vector for difference between means
gn<-tapply(group,group,length) # group sizes
e<-resid(lm.gp)
E<-t(e)%*%e
n<-nrow(e)
k<-lm.gp$rank
V<-(1/(n-k))*E # This is the pooled within-group vcv

d<-gp.m.dif; dim(d)<-c(1,length(d))

D<-d%*%solve(V)%*%t(d) # Squared Mahalanobis Distance

H.T2<-(gn[1]*gn[2])/(gn[1]+gn[2])*D # Hotelling T2

F<-(gn[1]+gn[2]-2-1)/((gn[1]+gn[2])*2)*H.T2 # Convert to an F value

P<-df(F,2,(gn[1]+gn[2]-2-1)) # P-value

P
```

```{r data measured AAs}
df<-read.csv("data/CSIA samples_update.csv")

# format metadata
make.fac<-c("species", "batch", "coral.ID", "glass.tube.ID", "sample.ID", "fraction", "AA", "AA.short")
df[make.fac]<-lapply(df[make.fac], factor) # make all these factors

df$depth.ft<-as.numeric(df$depth.ft)

# make a meter column
df<- df %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(depth.m = depth.ft*0.3048)

df$depth.bin<-ifelse(df$depth.ft<7, "shallow",
                    ifelse(df$depth.ft>17, "deep", "intermediate"))

df$depth.bin<-factor(df$depth.bin, levels=c("shallow", "intermediate", "deep"))
                    
# remove unwanted AAs
notwanted.AAs<-c("Met", "Nor", "Ami")

df<-df %>% 
  dplyr::filter(!as.factor(AA.short) %in% notwanted.AAs)
df<-droplevels(df)

# get categories
df$AA.cat<-ifelse(df$AA.short=="Ala" |df$AA.short=="Asp" |
                               df$AA.short=="Gly" | df$AA.short=="Glx" |
                               df$AA.short=="Pro" | df$AA.short=="Ser" | 
                               df$AA.short=="Tyr", "NESS", "ESS")

df$AA.short<-factor(df$AA.short, levels=c("Ala","Asp", "Glx", "Gly", "Pro", "Ser", "Tyr", "Ile", "Leu", "Lys", "Phe", "Thr", "Val"))


####### plot by EAA, with groups of sources and consumers

  facet_wrap(.~depth.bin)+
  ylim(-30,-3)+
  geom_boxplot(alpha=0.7)+
  #scale_fill_manual(values=c("gray90", "gray50", "gray10"))+ 
  scale_fill_manual(values=c("gray50", "mediumseagreen")) +

  ylab(expression(paste("AA  ", delta^{13}, C, " (\u2030)"))) +
  xlab("Amino Acids") +
  theme_classic()
```

```{r Blake plankton}
for(i in 1:length(BSO.plank.ESS$ID)){
  BSO.plank.ESS$Thr.n[i] <- (BSO.plank.ESS$Thr[i]-mean(as.numeric(BSO.plank.ESS[i,5:10])))
  BSO.plank.ESS$Val.n[i] <- (BSO.plank.ESS$Val[i]-mean(as.numeric(BSO.plank.ESS[i,5:10])))
  BSO.plank.ESS$Leu.n[i] <- (BSO.plank.ESS$Leu[i]-mean(as.numeric(BSO.plank.ESS[i,5:10])))
  BSO.plank.ESS$Ile.n[i] <- (BSO.plank.ESS$Ile[i]-mean(as.numeric(BSO.plank.ESS[i,5:10])))
  BSO.plank.ESS$Phe.n[i] <- (BSO.plank.ESS$Phe[i]-mean(as.numeric(BSO.plank.ESS[i,5:10])))
  BSO.plank.ESS$Lys.n[i] <- (BSO.plank.ESS$Lys[i]-mean(as.numeric(BSO.plank.ESS[i,5:10])))
}

BSO.ESS.norm<- BSO.plank.ESS %>%
  dplyr::select("sample.ID", "year", "location", "study", "Thr.n", "Val.n", "Leu.n", "Ile.n", "Phe.n", "Lys.n")

# combine the dataframes
BSO.merged<-merge(BSO.plank, BSO.ESS.norm)
write.csv(BSO.merged, "output/BSO.all.wide.csv")

BSO.ESS.norm.long<-melt(BSO.ESS.norm, idvar= c("sample.ID", "year", "location", "study"))

# rename factors
BSO.ESS.norm.long <- BSO.ESS.norm.long %>% 
       dplyr::rename("ESS.norm" = "variable")
BSO.ESS.norm.long <- BSO.ESS.norm.long %>% 
       dplyr::rename("d13C" = "value")
```

```{r combine it all}
# and mario

mario.ESS.norm.long$depth.bin<-"high.light"
```

```{r PCA}
PCA.dat<-comb.df.MC
PCA.dat<-PCA.dat %>% dplyr::select(-depth.m)

PCA.dat.wide<-reshape(PCA.dat, idvar= c("study", "location", "coral.taxa", "sample.ID", "batch", "fraction", "depth.bin", "light.depth"), timevar="ESS.norm", direction='wide')

#PCA.dat.wide$light.depth<-ifelse(PCA.dat.wide$fraction== "host" & PCA.dat.wide$depth.bin=="shallow", "high.light",
#                                 ifelse(PCA.dat.wide$fraction== "symb" & PCA.dat.wide$depth.bin=="shallow", "high.light",
#                                ifelse(PCA.dat.wide$fraction== "plank", "Plankton", "low.light")))

df.PCA.dat<-PCA.dat.wide %>% dplyr::select("d13C.Thr.n", "d13C.Val.n", "d13C.Leu.n", "d13C.Ile.n", "d13C.Phe.n", "d13C.Lys.n")

# run the PCA on scaled and centered data
set.seed(508)
PC.norm<- prcomp(df.PCA.dat, center = TRUE, scale= TRUE) 

PC.norm.summ<-summary(PC.norm) # 75% variation
plot(PC.norm, type="lines", main="PC.area eigenvalues")


###### plot for PCA 

## PC1 and PC2 by group and depth
PC.norm.plot <- ggbiplot(PC.norm, choices = 1:2, obs.scale = 1, var.scale = 1, 
                      groups=PCA.dat.wide$fraction,
                      ellipse = TRUE, circle = FALSE, alpha=0, ellipse.prob=0.95, ellipse.fill=NA, ellipse.linewidth=0.5) +
  geom_point(aes(shape=PCA.dat.wide$depth.bin, color=PCA.dat.wide$fraction), size = 4) +
  geom_vline(xintercept=0, linetype="dashed", color = "gray60")+
  geom_hline(yintercept=0, linetype="dashed", color = "gray60")+
  scale_x_continuous(breaks=pretty_breaks(n=5))+
  scale_color_manual(values=c("mediumorchid3", "sandybrown", "dodgerblue"))+
  scale_shape_manual(values=c(16,1,17))+
  scale_shape_manual(values=c(16,17,2))+
  ggtitle("ESS-normalized")+
   theme_classic()+
   theme(legend.text=element_text(size=10), 
    panel.background = element_rect(colour = "black", linewidth=1),
    legend.key = element_rect(color=NA, fill=NA),
    axis.ticks.length=unit(0.2, "cm"), 
    axis.text.y=element_text(margin=unit(c(0.5, 0.5, 0.5, 0.5), "cm")),
    axis.text.x=element_text(margin=unit(c(0.5, 0.5, 0.5, 0.5), "cm")))


## PC1 and PC2 (if want labels... labels = level)
PC.norm.study <- ggbiplot(PC.norm, choices = 1:2, obs.scale = 1, var.scale = 1, 
                      groups=PCA.dat.wide$light.depth, ellipse.fill=NA, ellipse.linewidth=0.5,
                      ellipse = TRUE, circle = FALSE, alpha=0, ellipse.prob=0.95)  + #labels=PCA.dat.wide$batch)  
  geom_point(aes(shape=PCA.dat.wide$fraction, color=PCA.dat.wide$light.depth), size = 4) +
  geom_vline(xintercept=0, linetype="dashed", color = "gray60")+
  geom_hline(yintercept=0, linetype="dashed", color = "gray60")+
  scale_x_continuous(breaks=pretty_breaks(n=5))+
  scale_color_manual(values=c("palevioletred2", "darkslategray3","seagreen4", "sandybrown","dodgerblue"))+
  scale_shape_manual(values=c(16,1,17))+
  ggtitle("ESS-normalized")+
   theme_classic()+
   theme(legend.text=element_text(size=10), 
    panel.background = element_rect(colour = "black", linewidth=1),
    legend.key = element_rect(color=NA, fill=NA),
    axis.ticks.length=unit(0.2, "cm"), 
    axis.text.y=element_text(margin=unit(c(0.5, 0.5, 0.5, 0.5), "cm")),
    axis.text.x=element_text(margin=unit(c(0.5, 0.5, 0.5, 0.5), "cm")))

## compile
grid.arrange(PC.norm.plot, PC.norm.study)
dev.copy(pdf, "figures/PCA.MC.all.pdf", width = 7, height = 10)
dev.off()
```

```{r PERMANOVA}
# groups with 3 groups (host, symb, plank)
PCA.esvi.fac<-PCA.dat.wide.esvi %>% dplyr::select(fraction)

# run PERMANOVA
set.seed(51)
PCA.esvi.norm.frac<-adonis2(df.PCA.dat.esvi ~ fraction, data = PCA.esvi.fac, 
                         permutations = 999, method = "euclidian", by = "terms")
PCA.esvi.norm.frac # fractions (host, symb, plankton) different at p=0.001, R2=0.51

### run pairwise for effects of fraction
set.seed(51)
pairwise.adonis(df.PCA.dat.esvi, factors = c(PCA.esvi.fac$fraction), sim.method = "euclidian", p.adjust.m = "none")
# all groups differ from each other, p=0.001 for plankton vs. host and symbiont, 0.034 for host/symb

###################################
###################################
# coral and symb only'
coral.esvi<-PCA.dat.wide.esvi[(!PCA.dat.wide.esvi$fraction=="plank"),]
coral.esvi$fraction<-droplevels(coral.esvi$fraction)

# make data and fact
PCA.coral<- coral.esvi %>% dplyr::select("d13C.Thr.n", "d13C.Val.n", "d13C.Leu.n", "d13C.Ile.n", "d13C.Phe.n", "d13C.Lys.n")
PCA.coral.fac<- coral.esvi %>% dplyr::select(fraction, depth.bin)

# run PERMANOVA
set.seed(51)
PCA.esvi.norm.frac<-adonis2(PCA.coral ~ fraction + depth.bin, data = PCA.coral.fac, 
                         permutations = 999, method = "euclidian", by = "terms")
PCA.esvi.norm.frac 
# host and symb slightly different at p=0.043, R2=0.13
# no difference across depth bins, p=0.910, R2=0.04
# no interaction: p=0.848, R2=0.04
```

```{r, symb only}
PC.norm.plot.symb
dev.copy(pdf, "figures/PCA.MC.symb.pdf", width = 5, height = 6)
dev.off()
```

### LDA -- ESVI only
```{r}
# full data = 'EAA.df.wide'
prod<- PCA.dat.wide.esvi[!(PCA.dat.wide.esvi$fraction=="host"),]
coral<- PCA.dat.wide.esvi[(PCA.dat.wide.esvi$fraction=="host"),]

prod$fraction<-droplevels(prod$fraction)
coral$fraction<-droplevels(coral$fraction)

#Run an LDA with a jackknifing model fit to look at error rate
#'CV = TRUE' makes the LDA run a jackknifed - leave one out - model fit
All.lda <- lda(fraction ~ d13C.Ile.n + d13C.Leu.n + d13C.Phe.n + d13C.Thr.n + d13C.Val.n + d13C.Lys.n, data = prod, CV = TRUE)

#Create a table which compares the classification from the LDA model to the actual classification
All.reclass <- table(prod$fraction, All.lda$class) #100% success

#Total percent of samples correctly classified is the sum of the diagonal of this table: 89%
sum(diag(prop.table(All.reclass)))

mean(All.lda$class==prod$fraction) # mean accuracy

#Percent of each producer Group correctly reclassified: 100% symb, 100% symb
diag(prop.table(All.reclass, 1))

####################
All.train <- lda(fraction ~ d13C.Ile.n + d13C.Leu.n + d13C.Phe.n + d13C.Thr.n + d13C.Val.n + d13C.Lys.n, data = prod)
All.train

#Write a csv file for the coefficients of LD1
lda.info <- as.data.frame(All.train$scaling)

coral.predict <- predict(object = All.train, newdata = coral)
coral.predict.data <- data.frame(sample.ID = coral$sample.ID, depth.bin = coral$depth.bin, 
                                 light.depth = coral$light.depth, fraction = "host",
                                coral.predict$class, coral.predict$x)

All.reclass <- table(coral$fraction, coral.predict$class) # 11 as symb, 1 as plankton
AllProdPredict <- data.frame(sample.ID = prod$sample.ID, prod$depth.bin, prod$light.depth, fraction = prod$fraction,
                             coral.predict.class= "prod", predict(All.train)$x)

# rename columns
colnames(AllProdPredict)<-c("sample.ID", "depth.bin", "light.depth", "fraction", "coral.predict.class", "LD1")

LDA.df<-rbind(AllProdPredict, coral.predict.data)
LDA.df$depth.bin<-as.character(LDA.df$depth.bin)
LDA.df$frac.depth<-ifelse(LDA.df$fraction=="host", LDA.df$depth.bin, 
                          ifelse(LDA.df$fraction=="symb", "symbiont", "plankton"))
LDA.df$frac.depth<-as.factor(LDA.df$frac.depth)
LDA.df$frac.depth<-factor(LDA.df$frac.depth, levels=c("plankton", "deep", "intermediate", "shallow", "symbiont"))

LDA.plot<-ggplot(LDA.df, aes(x=LD1, y=frac.depth, fill=frac.depth))+
  geom_boxplot(alpha=0.9, outlier.color=NA)+
  geom_jitter(aes(fill=frac.depth, shape=fraction), colour="black", size=3, show.legend = F) +
  geom_vline(xintercept=0, linetype="dashed", color = "gray60")+
  annotate(geom="text", label="Symbiont-Classified", x=-3, y=5.5, color="black", size=3) +
  annotate(geom="text", label="Plankton-Classified", x=2.5, y=5.5, color="black", size=3) +
  scale_fill_manual(values=c("dodgerblue", "indianred4", "khaki3", "coral2", "mediumseagreen"))+
  scale_shape_manual(values=c(21,8,24))+
  ylab("Consumer or Source") +
  xlab("LD1") +
  theme_classic() +
  guides(color = guide_legend(reverse=TRUE))+
  guides(fill = "none")

LDA.plot
dev.copy(pdf, "figures/LDA.pdf", width = 6, height = 5)
dev.off()

LDA.plot.alt<-ggplot(LDA.df, aes(x=LD1, y=interaction(fraction,depth.bin), fill=frac.depth))+
  geom_boxplot(alpha=0.9, outlier.color=NA)

```
